name: Temperance
concept: Least privilege and separation of duties
upright: Only what the task needs, only for as long as it needs it, and no single person holding every step of a sensitive process.
reversed: Standing admin rights for everyone, one clerk who orders, approves and pays, and roles that silently pile up power.
vision: An angel pours water between two cups, but only a single sip ever leaves the upper cup. The angel who fills a cup may never drink from it, and the jug tips only when a second angel grips its other handle. Wings sprout for each pour and molt the instant it ends. One foot stands on land, one in the river, and every spring a stranger borrows both and learns both shores. Up the path to a distant crown wait five gates: one opened by its owner's whim, one reading the label sewn in your collar, one admitting your uniform, one obeying the sign on its post, one weighing everything about you.
decode: Only a sip leaves the cup → least privilege: grant only the rights the task needs; need to know limits data access even for someone fully cleared.
The filler never drinks; two hands on one jug → separation of duties splits a task so fraud needs collusion; two-person control needs both present at once.
Wings that sprout for each pour and molt after → just-in-time privileged access: elevation granted for one task, then revoked automatically.
A stranger borrows both feet each spring → job rotation: cross-trained backups, and a successor who may uncover fraud the last holder concealed.
Owner's whim, collar label, uniform, posted sign, everything → DAC (owner), MAC (labels, clearances), RBAC (role), rule-based (global rules), ABAC (attributes).
facts: MAC compares labels: access needs a clearance that dominates the object's classification, plus need to know for its compartment. Users cannot change labels.
Every model except DAC is nondiscretionary: central policy, not the object's owner, decides access. DAC lets owners grant rights, usually through ACLs.
Privileged accounts: keep admin accounts separate from daily ones, vault and rotate their passwords, require MFA, record sessions and review every use.
trap: The collective keeps reading RBAC as rule-based. Role-based access follows your job role; rule-based applies global rules to every subject alike, such as a firewall's hours; ABAC weighs many attributes.
